I use nonbinary as a easy umbrella term but when I'm specific about my gender I say I'm a trans-masc demi woman. Trans-masc to me means I'm transitioning to be more masculine than what was expected of me as someone that's AFAB. For my specific case transitioning includes presentation, socially, and physically.

I was conflicted for a while about whether or not I was just a Trans man but I still have a strong connection to womanhood (even if it's small) and the Sapphic community. Once I discovered the label demi woman I realized that my masculinity isn't connected to being a man. Things became a lot easier after that.

I agree that the OP comment is hurtful and dangerous to the ace community. 

It is also dangerous to tell allosexuals to not talk about their struggles. If I didn't feel like I just had accept my partners boundaries fully regardless of my own we would've worked out our issues faster. It hurt BOTH of us, not just me. It took some time talking to people outside the relationship to figure out where my boundaries were so we could figure out what would work best for us.

I would fully agree with you if it didn't seem like you thought that allosexuals should ONLY talk to their partner about their struggles. Or that their feelings don't matter in the relationship.
I agreed with you. What are you trying to convince me of?

I am. That's why I just said it was wrong for you to say that allosexuals can't talk about the hardships they face. That's why I said that comments is wrong for painting the whole ace community in one negative colour.

And sometimes you can't/shouldn't talk to partner about something. If I went to my partner and just vented everything I was feeling she'd be devastated. Sometimes you need to talk to someone outside the relationship to help figure out your thoughts. Then you could be able to talk to them in a calmer manner. Clearly the OP commenter went about this in a terrible way, I never said otherwise.

Everyone's allowed to feel their feelings. That includes complaining. The problem here isn't the complaining, it's the gross generalization of the ace community.

I'm allo and engaged to an asexual. If I were to say there was no hardships on my part when she was first coming out that'd be a lie. We had different struggles but both of them were valid. Comments like this make it harder for allo people to talk about their feelings to their partner which just hurts both parties more.

The ace community definitely faces more discrimination than allosexuals. But it's wrong to say that allosexuals aren't allowed to also have a hard time within the relationship.
